analysis.investment_thesis: Godrej Agrovet scores poorly on both Magic Formula metrics — Earnings Yield of ~6.2% (EBIT INR 821 Cr / EV INR 13,212 Cr) is barely half the 12% minimum threshold, and ROCE of 16.6% falls below the 20% "good business" bar. You're paying a full price for a mediocre-return agri-business with thin 6.8% operating margins.
key_strengths: EBITDA CAGR of 17.2% over 9 years — operating leverage improving
Godrej brand + promoter holding of 67.65% provides governance anchor
FCF turned strongly positive in 2025 (INR 758 Cr) after years of destruction
key_risks: Earnings Yield ~6.2% — EV of INR 13,212 Cr is expensive for EBIT of only INR 821 Cr
Borrowings surged from INR 1,416 Cr (2024) to INR 2,159 Cr (2025), D/E at 1.11x
Net profit CAGR only 4.9% over 9 years despite 10.7% revenue growth — value leakage
red_flags: Equity dropped INR 707 Cr in one year (2,517→1,810 Cr in 2025) — unexplained capital reduction
OCF was negative in 2021 and 2022; FCF negative 3 of last 5 years — poor capital discipline
Operating margin of 6.84% — commodity-like agri business with no pricing power moat
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula: EV = Market Cap (INR 11,853 Cr) + Total Debt (INR 1,396 Cr) – Cash (INR 37 Cr) = INR 13,212 Cr. EBIT (Operating Income 2025) = INR 821 Cr. Earnings Yield = 821/13,212 = 6.2% — well below the 12% threshold where Greenblatt's formula starts getting interesting. ROCE of 16.6% is also sub-standard for Magic Formula quality (needs >20%). Both legs of the formula fail simultaneously, which is the clearest AVOID signal in this framework.

The business itself has structural issues: six operating segments (animal feed, palm oil, crop protection, dairy, poultry, chemicals) create complexity without the capital-light moat needed for high ROIC. The alarming jump in borrowings to INR 2,159 Cr alongside the unexplained INR 707 Cr equity drop in FY2025 warrants scrutiny before any investment. At 16.2x EV/EBITDA and 25.7x P/E, the market is pricing in growth that a 4.9% net profit CAGR over nine years doesn't justify.
